stem.en: Protium, deuterium and tritium are all isotopes of hydrogen. They have 1 proton each, with 0, 1 and 2 neutrons. Why do they have the same chemical properties?

text.en: They have the same number of electrons and the same electronic configuration.
They have the same mass number, so they react in the same way.
Neutrons decide the chemical properties, and all neutrons are alike.

explanation.en: Each isotope has 1 proton and so 1 electron, in the K shell, and chemical properties depend mainly on the valence electrons. Option b is wrong because their mass numbers are different: 1, 2 and 3. Option c is wrong because neutrons change the mass and not the chemistry.

hints.en: Which part of an atom takes part in a reaction? Do the three isotopes differ in that part?
